title: Bakery Line
statement: Customers wait in a line at a bakery. `loaves[i]` is how many loaves customer `i` wants. The baker serves one loaf per minute to the customer at the front; if that customer still wants more, they go to the back of the line. Customers who have all their loaves leave. Return the minute (counting from 1) when customer `k` gets their last loaf.

keyPoints: The line is first in, first out: take from the front, add to the back
Store customer indices in a queue; each minute, serve the front customer and lower their count
If their count is 0 and they are customer k, return the minute; if it is above 0, put them at the back
A direct count also works: customers before k take at most loaves[k] minutes, customers after k at most loaves[k] - 1
answerKey.timeComplexity: O(total loaves) for the simulation, O(n) for the direct count
answerKey.spaceComplexity: O(n) for the queue, O(1) for the direct count
edgeCases: Others want fewer loaves than k
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Simulate with array.shift(): correct, but each shift costs O(n)

hints: Who is served next, and where does a customer go if they still want loaves?
Use a queue of customer positions. In JavaScript, a head index avoids the slow shift().
Count minutes as you serve. Stop when customer k's count reaches 0.
